claims.statement: Galpi is a local-first macOS desktop app that records or imports meeting audio, runs speaker-diarized Korean transcription locally, and optionally produces Korean meeting minutes Markdown via an OpenAI-compatible API; it is a 0.1.0 development build shipping only for Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 14+ with an unsigned, not-yet-notarized DMG.

Galpi spans three runtimes — the TypeScript webview rooted at src/ (domain contracts, pure state machines, controllers, DOM UI, TauriBackend with Zod parsing at the edge), the Rust/Tauri host rooted at src-tauri/src/ (window, settings, secrets, CoreAudio recording, worker process supervision, Application facade over ports), and the Python sidecar rooted at worker/galpi_worker/ (Qwen3 and WhisperX engines, pyannote diarization, minutes refinement).

The three runtimes connect through exactly two channels: Tauri IPC (invoke inbound, job-event/recording-event outbound) between webview and host, and a versioned JSONL-over-stdout protocol (v/seq/type envelope, PROTOCOL_VERSION 1) between host and worker subprocess; transcription and diarization stay local and only an explicit AI-minutes run sends data to an external API.

Development requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon, Rust 1.88+ (the MSRV enforced in src-tauri/Cargo.toml), Bun 1.3+ (packageManager pinned to bun@1.3.14), and Tauri CLI 2.11.4, installed with `cargo install tauri-cli --version 2.11.4 --locked`; the boot commands are `bun install` then `bun run dev`.

No global Python, ffmpeg, or WhisperX install is needed for development: `bun run dev` (mapped in package.json to `cargo tauri dev`) triggers `bun run sidecar:stage && bun run vite:dev` via beforeDevCommand in tauri.conf.json, which stages the verified arm64 uv binary and the Python worker before the host launches; the same staging runs before production builds via beforeBuildCommand.

scripts/stage-sidecars.ts downloads the pinned arm64 uv archive (uv 0.12.5), verifies SHA-256 checksums of both the archive and the extracted binary before installing src-tauri/binaries/uv-aarch64-apple-darwin, and copies worker/galpi_worker (skipping __pycache__ and .pyc) plus the four requirements files (requirements.txt/.lock, requirements-qwen3.txt/.lock) into src-tauri/resources/worker for bundling.

The Vite dev server serves the UI on port 1420 with --strictPort, matching the devUrl in tauri.conf.json that the Tauri host loads; vite.config.ts builds with target safari17 because the window ships inside WKWebView on macOS 14+.

First-run engine preparation happens inside the app: open Settings, save a Hugging Face token if the pyannote diarization model needs a first download, then press 로컬 엔진 준비; the first prepare installs an app-private Python 3.12 environment and downloads several GB of models, a failed prepare is safely resumable from the same button, and the two engine presets install into separate virtualenvs so preparing one never affects the other.

Bun is the only supported verification driver — run `bun test`, never `npm test` — enforced by engines.bun >= 1.3.0 and packageManager: bun@1.3.14 in package.json, which is the canonical command map for every verification workflow.

The gate commands are: `bun run check` (architecture:check fence, then biome lint, then tsc --noEmit), `bun test` (frontend unit and happy-dom DOM tests), `bun run check:rust` (cargo fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test --all-targets, all via --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml), `bun run check:worker` (uvx ruff check, uvx ruff format --check, and PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m unittest discover over worker/tests), and `bun run check:all` chaining check, bun test, check:rust, and check:worker.

CI runs three parallel macos-15 jobs (frontend, rust, worker) on every push to main and every pull request, mirroring the per-runtime gates on the platform the app ships for; the tag-triggered release workflow only packages the DMG and runs none of the check gates.

The worker protocol is one change set: the Python EventWriter events in worker/galpi_worker/protocol.py, the Rust parser in src-tauri/src/domain/worker.rs, the frontend event schema, and the job reducer must change in the same commit — never change a protocol version, event, or field in Python alone.

User-facing copy is Korean (button labels like 전사 시작, output names like _화자별.txt) while protocol and error identifiers remain stable ASCII (event type values, AppError codes like IO_ERROR); neither side is translated into the other.

One dependency rule applies across all three runtimes: dependencies point inward to domain, ports are owned by the consuming inner layer and implemented by adapters, and framework code (Tauri, Zod, CPAL, tokio::process) lives only in adapters and composition; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is normative, and scripts/check-architecture.ts (run as `bun run architecture:check`, the first step of `bun run check`) is the executable fence that outranks prose claims.

The Tauri inbound surface is seventeen #[tauri::command] functions (diagnose_environment, prepare_environment, hugging_face_token_stored, save_hugging_face_token, load_assistant_settings, save_assistant_api_key, save_assistant_settings, save_engine_preset, refine_transcript, start_transcription, import_transcript, cancel_job, open_artifact, reveal_output_directory, start_recording, stop_recording, cancel_recording), all defined in src-tauri/src/adapters/inbound/tauri.rs, registered in composition.rs's generate_handler list, and delegated to the Application facade over the seven ports.

The generated trees in .gitignore — node_modules/, dist/, src-tauri/target/, src-tauri/gen/, src-tauri/binaries/, src-tauri/resources/worker/, and **/__pycache__/ — are not source; the staged worker copy under src-tauri/resources/worker/ must never be edited directly (edit worker/ and let staging copy it), and generated build output must not be committed.

The project carries its own agent documentation: AGENTS.md at the repo root plus nested src-tauri/AGENTS.md and worker/AGENTS.md, and the .issueops/ family (CONSTITUTION.md as the session-start baseline, TESTING.md before writing tests, ADR.md for structural decisions, CAUTIONS.md for recurring traps, plus AGENT_WORKFLOW, ARCHITECTURE, COMMIT_POLICY, CONVENTIONS, OPERATIONS, TECH_STACK) read selectively per task; source code and current command output remain the final authority over these docs.

Frontend work must subscribe to Tauri events before invoking the operation that emits them, and IPC-bound behavior must be expected to be dead in a plain browser (the DOM renders but every invoke/listen rejects) — a recorded project caution with its resolution in .issueops/cautions/.

Layering and boundary questions route to the architecture pages and the normative docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, resolved by running `bun run architecture:check` after any code move; the executable fence defines where code may live, including that Tauri commands stay in the inbound adapter, composition belongs to composition.rs, and process primitives stay in the process adapter.

Workflow tasks route to dedicated pages: microphone recording to workflows/recording (the CPAL NativeRecorder in src-tauri/src/adapters/outbound/recording/), AI minutes refinement to workflows/ai-minutes (worker refine.py pipeline plus the host refinement adapter), and first-run engine setup to workflows/engine-setup with concepts/engines-and-environment (setup.rs and preparation.py).

Tokens, keys, external APIs, and bundled runtimes route to integrations/external-services (SecretStore in src-tauri/src/adapters/outbound/secrets.rs, assistant_stream.py); building, staging, and releasing route to operations/build-and-packaging (stage-sidecars.ts, build-dmg.ts, release.yml); test architecture and what each gate covers route to testing/verification-gates.
